newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian stocks close lower after Dow drop.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian stocks close lower after Dow drop.

text.p: *Stocks settle lower by close, negative signals from Wall Street depress local traders. Volume 334.97 million shares, value A$764.06 million, 1,071 stocks traded, 295 steady, 236 up, 540 down.
The Australian share market closed lower on Thursday as local investors ignored positive employment data and followed their nervous U.S. counterparts out of equities.
At 4.10 p.m. (0510 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 19.7 points down at 2,339.6. December share index futures were down 16 points at 2,344, a 4.4 point premium to the index.

Brokers said the local market was set to fall after Wall Street tumbled 70 points, with only a mid-afternoon foray off its lows interrupting a day where the local benchmark index spent most of its time about 20 points off the pace.
"We tried to edge our way back up after the weak opening but it seems to have come in for a bit more selling," said a Brisbane-based dealer, adding that losses were widespread.
"There has been nothing too drastic. It's pretty well spread across the board," he said.
As bonds dipped, so did the banks which staged a strong but eventually futile rally in the mid-afternoon.
"They got back close (to square) but I think the bond market's negative reaction on the back of the U.S. bond market upset things a bit for them," the dealer said.
The banks and finance index lost 1.6 percent on the day, compared to a loss in the benchmark All Ordinaries index of just 0.8 percent.

In the industrials, construction group Leighton Holdings bucked the trend, closing 2.6 percent higher after it increased its work in hand by A$300 million with the purchase of a unit of government-owned telecommunications carrier, Telstra Australia.
The Lend Lease-managed property trust, Darling Park, made its debut and closed three cents off its A$1.00 issue price.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of about nine to four, while about 28 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Derivatives trade slowed after Wednesday's frantic rate-cut inspired activity.
Total options traded 32,788 (42,953)
Turnover in December SPI contracts totalled 7,284 (9,446)

In other local markets, Australian bond yields ended below the day's highs after another day of aggressive swings as the market continued to be battered by events offshore. The market awaits US releases on November CPI and retail trade later today.
By 4.50 p.m. (0550 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 7.39 percent.

The Australian dollar regained some poise through a calmer Thursday session as Japanese buying suggested yesterday's surprise rate cut had not completely dimmed the currency's appeal. Volumes were light but traders were impressed that heavy selling had been absorbed offshore while keeping US$0.7890 support intact, and felt a bounce to US$0.7950 was possible.

Sentiment was also shored by a firmer than expected set of labour data for November, which at least showed the economy was not in the sort of tailspin that would need further, immediate remedial action from monetary policy. By 4.50 p.m. (0550 GMT), the unit was at US$0.7923/28 from US$0.7915/20 late Wednesday.
